newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Start up of Saudi MTBE plant delayed to end May.
newsitem.headline: Start up of Saudi MTBE plant delayed to end May.

text.p: Saudi Petrochemical Co (Sadaf) has delayed the start up of its the new 700,000-tonne-per-year methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) plant in Al Jubail by 15 days to end May, sources close to the company said on Thursday.
"The start up has been delayed to end May because of technical problems," the source said.
Sadaf is a 50:50 joint venture between Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) and Royal Dutch Shell.
The new plant will raise Saudi Arabia's MTBE annual capacity to 2.6 million tonnes. MTBE is an additive and octane booster which makes gasoline burn cleanly.
The plant was originally scheduled to start up in February but this was delayed due to technical problems, industry sources said.
SABIC, which accounts for five percent of total world MTBE production, currently has three plants producing 1.9 million tonnes per year.
